description: Single-screen summary of a benchmark run: k6 load generator results, PostgreSQL, host metrics for every machine involved, and authentik's own CPU and heap profiles. Read it top to bottom - the k6 section says what the run achieved, the sections below say what stopped it going faster.

panels.title: Test summary (k6)
panels.description: Headline results for the selected scenario and time range.
Completed login flows per second - one k6 iteration is one full flow.
panels.title: Logins/s

panels.description: HTTP requests per second across all VUs. A login flow is several requests.
panels.title: Requests/s

panels.description: Median HTTP request duration, from the native histogram.
panels.title: Latency p50

panels.description: 95th percentile HTTP request duration.
panels.title: Latency p95

panels.description: 99th percentile HTTP request duration.
panels.title: Latency p99

panels.description: Share of requests k6 did not consider a valid response. Broken down by k6 error code below.
panels.title: Error rate

panels.description: Pass rate of the in-test assertions (status is 200, login completed).
panels.title: Checks passed

panels.description: Total completed login flows over the dashboard time range.
panels.title: Logins in range

panels.description: Login flows and HTTP requests per second. The ratio between the two is the number of requests a flow takes.
panels.title: Throughput

panels.description: Active VUs against the configured ceiling. k6 reports these without scenario labels, so they are not filtered by $scenario.
panels.title: Virtual users

panels.description: Per-request latency. Percentiles share one blue ramp (p50 nearest the background, p99 brightest); the mean is a different kind of statistic so it gets its own hue.
panels.title: HTTP request duration

panels.description: End-to-end time for a whole login flow, i.e. one k6 iteration. This is the number that matters to a user signing in.
panels.title: Login flow duration

panels.description: Full latency distribution over time, straight from the k6 native histogram. Bands that drift upward show the target degrading; a second band appearing means a bimodal response.
panels.title: Request duration distribution

panels.description: Everything in a request other than waiting for the server to think. Kept separate from the duration panel because these are microseconds while waiting time is seconds. Rising 'blocked' means the load generator is out of connections.
panels.title: Connection & transfer time (p95)

panels.description: HTTP status codes returned to k6. The login flow ends in a 302 redirect, so 200s and 302s should track each other.
panels.title: Requests by status

panels.description: Failed requests split by k6 error code. 1050/1211/1212 are client or connection level, 14xx/15xx mirror the HTTP status the server returned.
panels.title: Errors by k6 error code

panels.description: Bytes on the wire as measured by the load generator.
panels.title: Data throughput
PostgreSQL
panels.description: postgres_exporter on the authentik host. Scoped to the $db database.
Backends in use as a share of max_connections. Saturation here caps throughput no matter how fast the queries are.
panels.title: Connection usage

panels.description: Committed transactions per second.
panels.title: Transactions/s

panels.description: Rolled back transactions per second. Sustained rollbacks under load usually mean application errors, not contention.
panels.title: Rollbacks/s

panels.description: Share of block reads served from shared buffers rather than the OS or disk.
panels.title: Cache hit ratio

panels.description: Rows returned to the client per second.
panels.title: Rows fetched/s

panels.description: On-disk size of the benchmarked database.
panels.title: Database size

panels.description: Backends by state. A wall of 'idle in transaction' points at the application holding transactions open; 'active' climbing to max_connections is real database saturation.
panels.title: Connections by state

panels.description: Commit and rollback rate.
panels.title: Transactions

panels.description: Rows scanned versus rows actually handed back. A large gap between the two means queries are reading far more than they need.
panels.title: Rows read/s

panels.description: Write activity. Kept on its own axis because it runs orders of magnitude below the read rate.
panels.title: Rows written/s

panels.description: Dips mean the working set stopped fitting in shared_buffers.
panels.title: Buffer cache hit ratio

panels.description: Held locks by mode, zero-valued modes filtered out. Growing exclusive locks alongside flat throughput means contention.
panels.title: Locks by mode

panels.description: Age of the oldest open transaction. Long transactions hold back vacuum and inflate dead tuples.
panels.title: Longest transaction age

panels.description: Should be flat at zero. Anything here is a correctness problem in the workload, not a tuning issue.
panels.title: Deadlocks & conflicts/s

panels.description: Requested checkpoints outpacing timed ones means WAL is filling faster than checkpoint_timeout, which adds write stalls.
panels.title: Checkpoints/s

panels.description: Who is doing the writing. Buffers written 'by backend' mean queries are flushing pages themselves instead of leaving it to the background writer.
panels.title: Buffers written/s

panels.description: Write-ahead log on disk.
panels.title: WAL size

panels.description: Tables the workload is scanning end to end. High rates on a large table are the usual sign of a missing index.
panels.title: Top tables by sequential scans/s

panels.description: Dead row versions waiting on vacuum. Growth through a run means autovacuum is not keeping up with the churn.
panels.title: Top tables by dead tuples
Hosts (node_exporter)
panels.description: Every benchmark host. Blue is the authentik target, orange the k6 load generator, green the metrics box - the same colours in every panel.
Non-idle CPU across all cores. If the target host pins at 100% the benchmark is measuring the CPU, not authentik.
panels.title: CPU utilisation

panels.description: 1-minute load average divided by core count, so 1.0 means fully committed regardless of host size. Above 1.0 there are runnable tasks waiting.
panels.title: Load average, per core

panels.description: Memory in use excluding reclaimable cache.
panels.title: Memory used

panels.description: Steal is CPU the hypervisor took away - it invalidates run-to-run comparisons. Iowait is time blocked on storage.
panels.title: CPU steal & iowait

panels.description: PSI: fraction of wall time at least one task spent waiting on CPU. More honest than utilisation once a host is oversubscribed.
panels.title: CPU pressure stall

panels.description: Rising context switches with flat throughput means time is going into scheduling rather than work.
panels.title: Context switches/s

panels.description: Bytes read from disk.
panels.title: Disk read throughput

panels.description: Bytes written to disk - mostly WAL and checkpoints on the database host.
panels.title: Disk write throughput

panels.description: Completed read and write operations per second.
panels.title: Disk IOPS

panels.description: Fraction of wall time the device had I/O in flight. Approaching 1.0 means the disk is the bottleneck.
panels.title: Disk busy

panels.description: Inbound traffic on physical interfaces; container veth and bridge devices are excluded.
panels.title: Network received

panels.description: Outbound traffic on physical interfaces.
panels.title: Network transmitted

panels.description: Retransmitted segments. Non-zero values mean the network is adding latency the target is not responsible for.
panels.title: TCP retransmits/s

panels.description: Connections dropped because the accept queue was full - the classic symptom of a server that cannot accept as fast as k6 connects.
panels.title: Listen queue drops/s

panels.description: Sockets in use and in TIME_WAIT. A large TIME_WAIT pool can exhaust ephemeral ports on the load generator.
panels.title: TCP sockets in use

panels.description: Runnable and uninterruptible-sleep process counts. Blocked processes point at storage, not CPU.
panels.title: Processes

panels.description: Real filesystems only. A run that fills the disk fails in confusing ways.
panels.title: Filesystem used
Profiles (Pyroscope)
panels.description: Continuous profiles pushed by authentik. Blue is the server component, orange the worker. Flame graphs follow the dashboard time range, so narrow it to a single run before reading them.
CPU nanoseconds sampled per component. Read it against the k6 throughput panel: CPU that climbs while throughput flattens is where the run stopped scaling.
panels.title: CPU time by component

panels.description: Live heap per component. A ramp that never comes back down across a run is a leak rather than load.
panels.title: Heap in use by component

panels.description: Where the server component spent CPU over the selected range.
panels.title: CPU - server

panels.description: Where the worker component spent CPU over the selected range.
panels.title: CPU - worker

panels.description: Live heap by allocation site - what is still retained.
panels.title: Heap in use - server

panels.description: Total bytes allocated by site, including memory already freed. This is the allocation-pressure view, and the usual place GC overhead shows up.
panels.title: Allocations - server

list.description: Filters the k6 panels to one or more scenarios.
